title: THE FIGHT CARD · TEN ROUNDS, TEN WEAPONS
vibe: yellow-plus · 45 minutes · day one back on home iron · no treadmill, by design
why: You said two things and both of them shaped this. First: you'll trade tempo miles for this kind of work. Taken — every prescribed training day since July 29th has carried a run block, and today has none. Zero treadmill. Your legs flew twenty hours yesterday and they get to sit this one out. Second, and louder: the kettlebell exercises have gone stale. That's a fair hit. Pull the log and the same seven movements keep showing up — clean, press, swing, snatch, row, squat, carry. So today is built as a boxing card: ten rounds, and every round is a different weapon. EIGHT of the ten have never appeared anywhere in this program. Not a new arrangement of the old ones — genuinely new movements. The clock is new too: no EMOM, no ladder, no lap count. Fighter's rounds, 2:30 of work and 30 seconds in the corner, and effort is counted in REPS BANKED across the whole card. The tradition behind it is one this log has never drawn from — Ross Enamait's fight-camp work capacity, whose whole thesis is that variety IS the training stimulus. And one more thing from Singapore: you pressed a 44 lb bell and front squatted a 97 lb pair over there. Your home pair is 80 lb and your light bell is 35. Every tool in this house is now lighter than what you just handled, so the rep counts are written high on purpose.

blocks.title: WARM-UP · DAY A · SPINE, SHOULDERS, TRAVEL DECOMPRESSION
blocks.meta: ~6 min · Moves Method Day A · ONE PASS · biased to twenty hours in a seat

items.name: DECOMPRESS THE SPINE · one pass
items.detail: Jefferson curl, slow, 5 reps — roll down one vertebra at a time, roll up the same way · thoracic rotations on all fours, 8 per side · cat-cow ×10. Yesterday was a plane seat. Flexion and rotation first, before anything gets loaded overhead.

items.name: SHOULDERS · one pass
items.detail: Towel dislocates ×15 · shoulder extensions behind the back, 30 sec · scap push-ups ×10 · wrist rocks 30 sec each direction. This card is almost entirely shoulders, elbows and grip — three of today's ten rounds put a bell over your head from a dead stop, and one of them does it sitting on the floor. Open the shoulders properly.

items.name: HIPS · quick
items.detail: Half-kneeling hip flexor stretch 30 sec per side · 10 slow bodyweight hinges. No squatting today, but the hip flexors have been folded up since yesterday morning. Unfold them.

blocks.text: Day A off the Moves Method menu — an upper-body card gets the shoulder-and-spine day. Day B ran Wednesday, Day C Monday.

blocks.title: THE CARD · 10 ROUNDS · 2:30 WORK / :30 REST
blocks.meta: 30 MINUTES · 10 ROUNDS · one weapon per round · 2×40 lb pair · 35 lb · 50 lb DB
blocks.format: round-based fight card · 2:30 on, :30 in the corner · effort counted in TOTAL REPS BANKED, not rounds chosen or minutes held
blocks.workRest: Set a repeating interval: 2:30 work, 0:30 rest, 10 times through. One movement per round, worked for the whole 2:30 — break it up however you need to inside the round, but the bell doesn't leave your hand for long. Each round has a rep target. Hit it, write it down, move to the next weapon. Nothing repeats.

items.name: R1 · DOUBLE HIGH PULL · 2×40 lb · TARGET 45
items.detail: Both bells between the legs, hinge hard, and pull them to chest height with the elbows leading high and wide — a swing that keeps climbing. Explosive hips, no arm curl. Last seen in this log on July 28th. Sets of 8-10, this is the round that gets your heart rate up.

items.name: R2 · ★ SEE-SAW PRESS · 2×40 lb · TARGET 36 (18/side)
items.detail: NEW — never in this log. Both bells racked. Press the right overhead while the left stays racked; as the right comes down the left goes up. They pass each other. One is ALWAYS in the rack, which means your torso never gets a break from the offset load. Strict, no leg drive, no dip. Alternate continuously.

items.name: R3 · ★ BATWING ROW · 2×40 lb · TARGET 30
items.detail: NEW — never in this log. Hinge to a flat back, row BOTH bells to your ribs, and HOLD for a two-count with the shoulder blades crushed together before lowering. The hold is the exercise. Dan John's rule: if you can't pin the blades for two full seconds, the weight is moving you. Slow, mean reps.

items.name: R4 · ★ DEAD-STOP ALTERNATING SWING · 35 lb · TARGET 60
items.detail: NEW variant. The bell parks on the floor between EVERY rep — no backswing, no rebound, no chain of momentum. Hike it once, one swing to chest height, park it, switch hands, again. Killing the stretch reflex turns each rep into a pure standing-start hip snap. Sixty of them. This is your only hinge volume today and it costs your legs almost nothing.

items.name: R5 · ★ Z PRESS · 35 lb · TARGET 30 (15/side)
items.detail: NEW — never in this log. Sit on the floor, legs straight out in front, feet together, torso vertical with no support of any kind. Clean the bell to the rack and strict press it. With the legs taken out of the equation there is nowhere to cheat from — every ounce of stability comes from your midline and hips. This will feel harder at 35 lb than a 44 lb standing press did in Singapore. That is the point.

items.name: R6 · ★ BOTTOMS-UP CLEAN · 35 lb · TARGET 40 (20/side)
items.detail: NEW — never in this log. Clean the bell and catch it UPSIDE DOWN, handle in a crushing grip, bell balanced above your fist. Any wobble and it folds over. Pure grip, forearm and shoulder-packing work — your confirmed favorite family, in a form you've never done. Park it, reset, go again. Switch hands every 5.

items.name: R7 · ★ SKULLCRUSHER → CLOSE FLOOR PRESS · 50 lb DB · TARGET 36
items.detail: NEW — the skullcrusher has never appeared here. On your back, DB in both hands over the chest. Six reps bending ONLY at the elbows, lowering the head of the bell toward your forehead. Then six close-grip floor presses, elbows tucked to the ribs. Alternate 6 and 6 for the round. Direct triceps work, which this program has essentially never given you.

items.name: R8 · ★ DOUBLE UPRIGHT ROW · 2×40 lb · TARGET 45
items.detail: NEW — never in this log. Standing, bells in front of the thighs, pull them straight up the body to collarbone height with the elbows above the wrists the whole way. Slow on the way down. Delts and traps, direct and unglamorous. If the shoulders pinch, stop the pull at sternum height and keep going.

items.name: R9 · ★ DEFICIT PUSH-UP ON THE BELLS · bodyweight · TARGET 50
items.detail: NEW here. Hands on the two 40s, handles parallel, and drop your CHEST BELOW the handles on every rep. The extra four inches of range is what makes it different from anything you did in Singapore. Fifty of them, in whatever chunks the round allows. Keep the ribs down — the bells will punish a sagging plank.

items.name: R10 · ★ THE GRIP ROUND · 2×40 lb + 50 lb DB · 5 × 0:30 HOLDS
items.detail: NEW — the bear hug has never appeared here. Last round, no reps, just hold on. Alternate every 30 seconds: FARMER HOLD, both 40s at your sides, shoulders packed, standing tall — then BEAR-HUG HOLD, the 50 crushed against your chest with both forearms, squeezing it so hard it can't slide. Five holds, 2:30 total, hands screaming. Fitting way to end a card.

items.name: THE STANDARD · 372 REPS BANKED
items.detail: GREEN: all ten rounds at the written targets = 372 reps plus the grip round. YELLOW: run all ten rounds and take roughly 80% on each target — 36/28/24/48/24/32/28/36/40 — never drop a round. Tell me the number you actually banked and which round broke you; that's what sets the next card.

blocks.noteGreen: Eight of these ten movements have never appeared in this program. That is deliberate and it is the whole point of today. Written at the top of the range because your home 40s are now lighter than the Singapore tools you handled — the load isn't the challenge here, the clock and the novelty are.
blocks.text: Ross Enamait's fight-camp thesis, verbatim in spirit: 'We are not looking to adapt to a particular routine or training style. It is important to incorporate variety to prevent staleness.' Ten rounds, ten weapons, nothing repeated.

blocks.title: NO TREADMILL TODAY · ON PURPOSE
blocks.meta: 0 min prescribed · first training day since JULY 29 with no run block

items.name: THE TRADE, HONORED
items.detail: You offered to scale back the tempo running in exchange for this kind of session. Deal. Every single prescribed training day from July 29 through Wednesday carried a run — tempo, fartlek, mile repeats, incline, gauntlet legs, hard 800s. Today carries none. Your legs sat in a metal tube for twenty hours yesterday and every one of the ten rounds above is built to leave them alone.

items.name: AND YET · your miles are still yours
items.detail: If you get on the belt today anyway, that has always been your baseline, never a deviation. Just keep it easy — 7.3 to 7.6 on the console — and do it AFTER the card, not before. Nothing in these 45 minutes needs it.

blocks.text: Running comes back tomorrow, in shape rather than in miles.

blocks.title: THE CHAMPIONSHIP ROUNDS · 2 × 2:30
blocks.meta: 6 MINUTES · 2 ROUNDS of 2:30 work / :30 rest · 35 lb + bodyweight
blocks.format: round-based midline · same clock as the card · three new movements, cycled continuously inside each round
blocks.workRest: Two more rounds on the same interval. Cycle the three movements continuously for the full 2:30, then 30 seconds down, then round two.

items.name: ★ TURKISH SIT-UP · 35 lb · 6 per side
items.detail: NEW. The first half of a get-up and nothing else. Flat on your back, bell locked out over the shoulder, opposite knee bent — sit up to the elbow, then to the tall hand, then reverse it under control. Eyes on the bell the whole time. All the get-up's midline work in a fraction of the time.

items.name: ★ BODY SAW · bodyweight · 10 reps
items.detail: NEW. Forearm plank on a smooth floor with socks, or feet on a towel. Push back through the forearms so your whole body slides four to six inches toward your feet, then pull back to start. The plank never breaks — you're just making it longer and harder. Anti-extension under a moving lever arm.

items.name: ★ WINDSHIELD WIPER · bodyweight · 8 per side
items.detail: NEW. On your back, arms wide on the floor for anchor, legs up at 90 degrees, knees bent to start. Lower both legs slowly to the right without letting the opposite shoulder peel off the floor, then to the left. Rotation control — the one midline quality this program has trained the least.

blocks.text: Anti-extension and rotation control, on the same round clock as the card. Three movements, all three new.

blocks.title: COOLDOWN · 3 MIN

items.name: FOREARMS + ELBOWS · 60 sec
items.detail: Kneel, palms flat on the floor with fingers pointing back at your knees, sit back gently. Then flip to the backs of the hands. Bottoms-up cleans, batwing holds and a grip round earned this.

items.name: DOORWAY PEC + OVERHEAD REACH · 60 sec
items.detail: 30 seconds per side in the doorway after fifty deficit push-ups, then kneel and reach both arms long overhead onto a couch or bed, chest sinking. Undo the pressing.

items.name: BREATHE · 60 sec
items.detail: Flat on your back, knees bent, hand on your belly. Long slow nasal exhales. Day one back on home iron, and you spent every minute of it working. Welcome home.

blocks.text: No belt, no miles, no squats. Just ten rounds and ten new things.

timer.emomUnit: rounds of the card completed at full reps
